subject.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup

question: Should OpenClaw delete matching stale backup temp artifacts on backup startup after a grace window once the timestamped-output matcher is fixed, or should cleanup move behind a narrower explicit recovery path?
rationale: This PR changes backup startup from passive recovery to destructive cleanup of old partial backup artifacts, which is a compatibility and operator-policy choice that code inspection cannot settle alone.

options.title: Accept Guarded Startup Cleanup
options.body: Fix the timestamped-output matcher, keep the owner and grace-window guards, and treat stale OpenClaw backup temps as disposable crash recovery artifacts.

options.title: Use Explicit Recovery Only
options.body: Move stale backup cleanup behind a doctor or backup cleanup command so operators choose when partial artifacts are deleted.

options.title: Pause Cleanup Policy
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers do not want backup startup to delete prior-run artifacts automatically.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Startup Cleanup
recommendation.body: Fix the timestamped-output matcher, keep the owner and grace-window guards, and treat stale OpenClaw backup temps as disposable crash recovery artifacts.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the backup infra extraction and original backup CLI review context, which makes them the best available owner for the cleanup-policy choice.
